subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should OpenClaw support opt-in Feishu group per-sender dynamic agents/subagents with isolated workspaces, skills, memory, and lifecycle controls, and should that contract live in the Feishu plugin or a generic channel API?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the requested behavior changes channel routing, persistent session state, dynamic config writes, security boundaries, and user-specific memory semantics.

options.title: Design Opt-In Feishu Isolation
options.body: Define a Feishu-owned per-sender group isolation contract with explicit security defaults, quotas, cleanup, migration/doctor behavior, and focused live proof before implementation.

options.title: Use Existing Session Scopes
options.body: Keep current groupSessionScope plus DM dynamic agents as the supported path and document the limits while related narrower issues proceed.

options.title: Defer To Generic Channel API
options.body: Wait for a broader non-thread persistent-session and user-skill preference contract before adding Feishu-specific dynamic group subagents.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Feishu Isolation
recommendation.body: Define a Feishu-owned per-sender group isolation contract with explicit security defaults, quotas, cleanup, migration/doctor behavior, and focused live proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The package metadata names this handle as the Feishu plugin community maintainer, making them the best first routing point for the channel-specific product decision.
